messages:
Helen: Opening a focused PR to standardize SOC2 wording for audit exports and add Go + Ruby SDK examples. URL: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4991. Wanted quick legal/security sanity checks before requesting reviews.
Diego: Nice. What's the concise blurb we'll put at the top-level export section? Paste it here and I'll review for clarity.
Helen: Draft blurb:
"Audit exports provide event-level telemetry for tenant audits and operational troubleshooting. By default, personal identifiers (for example email addresses) are pseudonymized in exported artifacts. Tenants may request inclusion of original identifiers; such requests must be authorized and are recorded in the tenant audit trail. Retention: default 365 days; records under legal hold are retained until released. Exports are encrypted in transit and at rest. (See SOC2 control mapping appendix.)"
Priya: Legal: good start. Replace "may request" with "may request inclusion of original identifiers; such requests must be authorized and are recorded." Use "personal identifiers" not "PII". Also avoid words like "anonymous" unless irreversible.
Marco: Security: add a parenthetical clarifying mapping exports are limited to tenant admins and require explicit consent. Also add a sentence: "Pseudonymization is not a substitute for role-based access controls."
Helen: Updated the blurb accordingly. Also adding a compact retention matrix table (public-facing one-line): `default: 365d | legal-hold: indefinite until release | enterprise: negotiated` and linking to the detailed Data Retention Policy.
Diego: Can we include Go + Ruby SDK examples? Most migration docs have curl/python/node; some customers use Go/Ruby.
Helen: Yes, adding both. Go snippet:
```go
// export audit events with pseudonymization (Go SDK)
client.Audit.Export(ctx, &audit.ExportRequest{
    TenantID: "t_42",
    Since:    "2026-01-01",
    Pseudonymize: true,
})
```
Ruby snippet:
```ruby
# export with pseudonymization (Ruby SDK)
client.audit.export(tenant_id: 't_42', since: '2026-01-01', pseudonymize: true)
```
Marco: Looks good. Add a one-line migration note: old flag `redact_personal` -> new `pseudonymize`. Maybe include a quick sed example: `git grep -l "redact_personal" | xargs sed -i '' -e 's/redact_personal/pseudonymize/g'`
Helen: Adding that and a tiny CI test snippet suggestion to assert no email regex in pseudonymized output: `assert !output.match(/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/)` (language-agnostic).
Priya: Also add the requirement that inclusion of original identifiers must be recorded and tied to an approval ticket or signed consent; don't leave that implicit.
Helen: Will add: "Inclusion of original identifiers requires documented approval and is logged as part of the tenants audit trail; mapping exports are restricted to tenant admins."
Diego: Can we show a sample CSV row so product folks get the mapping? Make it short.
Helen: Sample CSV row added: `timestamp,tenant,actor,action,tokens,request_id`
`2026-02-20T08:21:00Z,t_42,end_user_pseudo_99,model.generate,64,req_x9y8`
Marco: Security nit: add a note that masking/pseudonymization reduces identifiability but is not equivalent to deletion; link to De-Identification Policy.
Helen: Added and linked. Also noticed the anchor for `audit-export-guidance` was changed in a previous refactor which broke the export-playbook link; fixing that anchor and adding a redirect in the PR.
docs-ci: docs-ci: lint OK; preview available at https://staging.redwood.ai/docs/audit-export (expires in 48h)
Priya: One last phrasing tweak: change "Tenants may request inclusion" -> "Tenants may request inclusion of original identifiers; such requests must be authorized and are recorded." Make sure that exact sentence is in the public doc.
Helen: Done. Pushed final changes and requested legal/security review on PR #4991. Will merge after approvals. Thanks all :sparkles:
